It would seem that two people of the same gender and different races would be much more biologically similar than two people of different genders but the same race.

The author is in fact right, and what bothers people about it is that they don't want to accept the natural conclusions of their own reasoning. If you're willing to accept that a person can be born with a mind that doesn't match his/her biological body, it follows, at least in theory, that a person could be born into the wrong race as well as into the wrong gender. Of course in this specific case one can justify the vitriol directed against Dolezal because she lied about it, but the progressive left are in for a rude awakening when someone publicly comes out as "transracial" openly without any deceit.

Indeed, both of these possibilities are actually even more profound when one ponders their implications: transgender people by their very existence disprove the assertion that gender is 100% a social construct; after all, if it is possible to be born with a gender different from one's sex, then gender exists from birth and cannot be purely constructed. Similarly, if it is possible to be born with a race that doesn't match one's body, this would also imply that race exists from birth and is also not a social construct.

I wonder how that actually applies in terms of biology. There have been reports that many transgender people who are born female experience "phantom limb" sensation in a non-existent penis. Their neurology does not match the rest of their physiology. They feel incomplete without the opposite genitals, similar to people with other forms of BDD feel incomplete with a leg, for example. In transgender people, they can't fix the 'software,' so they fix the 'hardware' to properly run the 'software.' I can't imagine that neurology/physiology connection would exist for someone who had the wrong color skin. Can it? I'd be interested in reading about it if it could.

Further, there are cognitive difference between the sexes. Brains are structured differently. I am curious how true that is towards race. I always hear that women evolved to be gatherers and men evolved to be hunters, so predispositions towards certain preferences or skills relate to that. Are there similarly significantly different cognitive predispositions between races?

Lastly, the parents are capable of producing a male or a female, and sometimes those hormones in the mother can get a little confused and mess up which part it's supposed to be developing. It's like the male biological switch was supposed to be switched during fetal development, but the female one got switched instead and the brain developed incorrectly for the genitals. However, two white parents don't have the capability of producing a black baby. It's not like the "black" switch is flipped instead of the "white" one. That black switch isn't there.

So the natural conclusions of my own reasoning allow for one but not another. I'm open to reliable readings that are able to be understood by someone without a hard science degree that would inform me more about these things one way or another, but based on my current understandings, this makes sense to me without (as far as I can tell) being inconsistent.
